epics.title: Podcast Media Hub
epics.jtbd: When a visitor wants to listen to the podcast, I want to browse episodes with detailed show notes and audio playback, so that I can consume the audio content directly.
requirements: R1: Visitor can see a list of available podcast episodes.
R2: Visitor can click an episode to view detailed show notes.
R3: Visitor can play the audio of the selected episode directly in the browser.
R4: Visitor receives visible feedback on audio playback progress, with the ability to pause and scrub.
R5: Visitor can navigate and use the player seamlessly on a mobile device.
R6: Visitor sees a clear error message and recovery option if the audio stream fails to load.
R7: The creation and publishing of podcast episodes is handled by an external system or manual database insert; this epic covers only read and playback functionality.

slices.title: Shared API Contract for Podcast Media
slices.jtbd: When implementing the podcast media backend and frontend, I want a shared API contract, so that both components can be developed in parallel against a consistent interface.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a podcast player requirement,
When defining the API contract,
Then the REST endpoints for listing and fetching episodes must be documented.
Given the API specification,
When building the UI and backend,
Then both must adhere to the defined DTOs for episodes, including media URLs and show notes.

slices.title: Database Schema and Persistence for Podcasts
slices.jtbd: When implementing podcast data storage, I want a structured schema for episodes, so that the podcast data is persisted reliably.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new podcast episode,
When saving it to the database,
Then it must store the title, show notes, media URL, and publication date.
Given existing podcast data,
When querying for episodes,
Then the data must be retrieved efficiently by publication date.

slices.title: Podcast Backend API
slices.jtbd: When implementing the podcast backend, I want an API to serve episodes, so that the frontend can fetch the catalog and media links.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an API request for episodes,
When the client requests the podcast list,
Then a paginated JSON response with episode details must be returned.
Given an API request for a specific episode,
When fetching by ID,
Then the full show notes and media link must be provided.

slices.title: Podcast UI Player
slices.jtbd: When implementing the podcast UI, I want a functional media player and episode list, so that visitors can browse, play, and read show notes.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the podcast page on a desktop or mobile device,
When a visitor clicks play on an episode,
Then the audio must begin playing with a visible scrub bar and pause control.
Given WCAG 2.1 level AA standards,
When rendering the player controls,
Then all buttons must be keyboard operable, clearly labeled, and have a 4.5:1 text contrast.
Given a failed media stream,
When the audio cannot load,
Then an error message is shown, offering a retry option without breaking the layout.

slices.title: QA Verification for Podcast Hub
slices.jtbd: When verifying the podcast hub, I want full test coverage across the stack, so that audio playback and browsing are proven to work end-to-end.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a running application instance,
When executing E2E tests,
Then the frontend must successfully render the episode list, load an audio stream, and handle playback controls.
Given the backend test suite,
When running integration tests,
Then the API must serve correct DTOs mapped from the database.
Given a missing audio file scenario,
When executing tests,
Then the frontend must visibly render the error state.

epics.title: Platform Telemetry and Measurement
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want to measure visitor engagement with my content and external links, so that I know if the site successfully drives interest in my work.
requirements: R1: Goal: Measure visitor engagement with podcast content to evaluate interest. Questions: How many times do visitors start playing episodes? Which episodes have the most playback sessions? Metric: Podcast playback initiation count by episode.

slices.title: Telemetry Backend API
slices.jtbd: When implementing the telemetry backend, I want an endpoint to receive engagement events, so that frontend playback actions are persisted.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an incoming telemetry event payload,
When the endpoint receives it,
Then the event is saved to the database without blocking the request.
Given a high volume of events,
When multiple clients send events,
Then the backend successfully queues or saves them with low latency.

slices.title: Telemetry Tracking Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the frontend telemetry, I want to fire an event upon podcast playback, so that the engagement metric is accurately recorded.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the podcast player,
When a user clicks play,
Then a telemetry event containing the episode ID must be dispatched.
Given the tracking system,
When the event fires,
Then it must not block or delay audio playback.

slices.title: QA Verification for Telemetry
slices.jtbd: When verifying telemetry, I want to ensure engagement events are captured properly, so that the engagement metric is reliable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a mock telemetry endpoint,
When triggering frontend playback,
Then an assertion must verify that exactly one 'play' event is dispatched with the correct episode ID.
Given a bulk batch of events,
When processing telemetry,
Then the events must map to the corresponding podcast IDs accurately.

epics.title: Initial Content and Acceptance
epics.jtbd: When receiving the delivered system, I want to see it populated with realistic content, so that I can verify all paths and features work end-to-end.
requirements: R1: System is seeded with at least three realistic podcast episodes containing real audio file URLs and actual show notes, enabling full path verification.

slices.title: Initial Podcast Content Seed
slices.jtbd: When initializing the database, I want realistic podcast episode seeds, so that acceptance testing can exercise the real UI.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a clean database deployment,
When running data migrations,
Then three full podcast episodes must be inserted, each with valid title, show notes, and test audio URLs.
Given the acceptance environment,
When loading the podcast player,
Then the content is immediately visible and playable without manual entry.
